hook.igCaptionLine1: Don't forward an AI summary until you watch this 📄
hook.igCaptionLine2: Every word can be true, and it can still send you the wrong way 👇

sources.claim: BBC study (Feb 2025): 51% of AI answers to news questions had significant issues; 19% of answers citing BBC content introduced factual errors (statements, numbers, dates); 13% of quotes from BBC articles altered or not in the article; ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Perplexity; reviewed by BBC journalists
Gemini said 'The NHS advises people not to start vaping, and recommends that smokers who want to quit should use other methods'; the NHS does recommend vaping as a method to quit smoking
sources.note: example listed in the same BBC release

sources.claim: EBU/BBC News Integrity in AI Assistants (Oct 2025): 3,000+ responses, 22 PSM orgs, 18 countries, 14 languages; 45% had at least one significant issue; 31% serious sourcing problems; 20% major accuracy issues
Just over a third of UK adults trust AI to produce accurate summaries, almost half of under-35s
sources.note: BBC audience research cited in the same release; optional on-screen footnote

sources.claim: Lesson content: four ways summaries go wrong (invented details, flipped meaning, wrong attribution, false certainty); 2-minute spot-check of the 2–3 claims you act on; ask for page numbers + keep the source's certainty; summaries drop caveats, conditions and dissent; 'What did you leave out…' question; phones-only / two-week holiday test / 2 of 5 designers example

teyro.outroHeadline: Use AI at work. Check it before you send.

lines.text: Don't forward an AI summary | until you *watch* this.
When the BBC checked AI answers about the news, | *more than half* had a significant problem.
And they read perfectly. | Let's follow one summary, | and catch every mistake.
This is Ada. | Her boss needs a forty-page report | summed up by nine. | Seconds later, | one clean paragraph.
It sounds great. | She's about to hit *forward*.
First, | why it sounds so sure. | AI doesn't look things up. | Like a very good autocomplete, | it writes the most likely next words.
Sounding right is its whole job. | So a wrong summary reads | *just as smoothly* as a right one.
Mistake one. | *The invented number.* | The summary says sign-ups rose thirty-two percent. | That number isn't in the report.
It filled a gap with something likely. | That's called a *hallucination*. | In the BBC study, | nearly one in five answers | added wrong facts, | numbers or dates.
Mistake two. | *The flipped not.* | The report: | the client did *not* approve the budget. | The summary: | the client approved it. | One word. | Opposite meaning.
Real example: | an assistant said the NHS tells smokers | to quit without vaping. | It actually *recommends* vaping.
Mistake three. | *The wrong person.* | Grace raised the risk. | The summary gives it to Sam.
Who said what gets lost all the time. | A bigger follow-up study found serious *sourcing* problems | in thirty-one percent of answers.
Mistake four. | *False certainty.* | The report: | a few users suggested dark mode. | The summary: | *users want* dark mode.
May becomes will. | Some becomes all. | A very different decision.
So does Ada have to read | all forty pages herself?
Quick thing. | This is straight out of AI at Work, | a beginner course on Teyro.
Short daily lessons. | Okay. | Forty pages? | No. | *Two minutes.*
Fix one. | *The two-minute check.* | Don't check every sentence. | Just the two or three claims | you'll act on.
Find each one in the report. | Check the number, | the not, | who said it, | and how *sure* it was.
Fix two. | *Ask for proof up front.* | Tell it: | only use claims from the text, | add page numbers, | and keep the report's certainty.
Now every claim points to a page. | Checking takes *seconds*.
Now here's the weird part. | A summary can be *a hundred percent accurate*, | and still mislead you.
Sign-ups went up. | True. | But only on phones, | in a two-week holiday test, | and two of five designers disagreed.
The summary kept the headline, | and dropped every *but*. | Every word was true. | The decision would be wrong.
So ask: | what did you leave out | that a careful reader would want to *know*?
To be fair, | most summaries are mostly right. | That's exactly why the wrong ones slip through.
So. | It sounds sure by design. | Check the numbers, | the nots, | the names, | the certainty. | Then ask what it *left out*.
Using AI at work is a skill. | You can learn it on Teyro.
AI at Work is sixty lessons, | from your first prompt | to checking AI answers.
Lessons run in four steps, | and you practise straight away, | with instant feedback.
Your streak grows every day, | and a freeze covers a busy one. | Weekly leagues, | Bronze to Diamond. | Daily quests and chests.
It plays like a game, | so you actually *finish*.
Trust the summary. | But check the *but*.
